Dirty soda in Santa Clara, Utah

Old orchards, Swiss pioneer roots and a main street lined with painted cows during Swiss Days. Dirty sodas built to order, real soft serve and fresh espresso for Santa Clara backyard receptions, open houses and family parties, from a retro trailer that comes to you.

The town the Swiss settlers built

Santa Clara is older than most of the county. It began as the headquarters of Jacob Hamblin's Indian Mission on the Santa Clara River, and then a company of Swiss converts was sent south to settle it. Weeks after they arrived, a long rain flooded the river and destroyed the fort and the first settlement, and the earlier settlers moved over to the land where the Swiss families had settled. The Swiss knew how to grow grapes, and the warm climate turned out to be ideal for fruit; the Washington County Historical Society says Santa Clara became the fruit and vegetable garden of the county, and fruit stayed the town's main living for more than half a century.

Swiss Days and Santa Clara Drive

The city's Swiss Days celebration honors those Swiss pioneers. The city describes a parade along Santa Clara Drive from the Jacob Hamblin Home to City Hall, pioneer activities at Heritage Square, live entertainment, local food and merchandise vendors, and decorated cows that residents and businesses display along Santa Clara Drive and in their yards. Vendors go through the city's own sign-up. If the trailer is ever part of a Swiss Days weekend, it will be because the city accepted us, and it will go on our stops list then. A private party at your own home is always an easy booking.

Family parties in a family town

Santa Clara still feels like the small town it grew from, and the parties we hear about here are family ones: graduation open houses, missionary farewells and homecomings, reunions, birthdays and the backyard reception after a wedding. Old orchard lots and big yards usually have room for the trailer. We need a flat spot a truck and trailer can pull into, close to your guests, and the trailer brings its own power and water. Kid sizes, zero-sugar sodas and caffeine-free lemonades and Italian sodas mean the grandparents and the toddlers both get something. See receptions and open houses and graduations and birthdays.

Wards, schools and teams

Wards and stakes book us for youth nights, ward parties and trek send-offs. Lava Ridge Intermediate is in Santa Clara, and west-side PTAs and booster clubs book teacher thank-yous, carnival nights and team fundraisers. If your activity is at a meetinghouse, the building's rules come first, so a covered tab with no sales is usually the simplest fit, or we can meet you at a park or a home. See church and school events and tournaments and team parties.

Santa Clara summers

Summer afternoons here regularly pass 100 degrees, so we plan around the heat: a morning open house with iced lattes and sweet-cream cold brew, or an evening party once the sun drops. Every drink is poured over nugget ice, and the soft-serve machine turns any soda into a float. For a midday event we'll suggest a short menu and a time window that keeps the line moving.

Next door: Ivins and St. George

Santa Clara and Ivins are next-door neighbors on the west side of the county, and the trailer covers both. Ivins started out as the Santa Clara Bench, and it has Kayenta and the red-rock resorts. Back toward town, Bloomington and Green Valley are on the southwest side, and St. George is where we open first.

Where you'll find us in Santa Clara

We're not open for public stops yet, and we won't make up a date. Public stops go on the homepage stops list and the live map once they're actually booked, and text and email alerts are coming soon. Until then, the fastest way to get the trailer to Santa Clara is to book it for your own event.

Questions

Santa Clara dirty soda FAQ

Do you come to Santa Clara?

Yes. Santa Clara is next door to St. George, where we open first. Send the date, place and head count and we'll reply with a price within one business day.

Will you be at Swiss Days?

Only if the city accepts us as a vendor, since Swiss Days vendors go through the city's own sign-up. We only list a public stop once it's booked. A private party at your home that weekend is easy to book.

Can you park at an older home or on a narrow street?

Usually. We need a flat spot a truck and trailer can pull into, like a driveway, a side lot or a wide street edge, close to your guests. Tell us about the spot and we'll plan it when we quote.

Can you come to a ward activity?

Yes. Ask your bishopric or building representative about the meetinghouse rules first; a covered tab with no sales is usually the simplest fit. A park or a member's home works well too.

Do you have drinks for kids and caffeine-free options?

Yes. Beach Babies kid sizes, soft-serve cones, zero-sugar sodas, and lemonades and Italian sodas with no caffeine.

When will the trailer be open?

We're not open for public stops yet, and we won't make up a date. Stops go on the homepage stops list and live map the minute they're booked. Private events are booking now.
